searchText: > Block number will probably stay inside of Eth1 block, likewise timestamp. hmm this seems long-term not the best approach though? Like, why do we need two number objects? `max_pow_block_num + slot` makes a lot of sense > GASLIMIT will now be decided on by validators or will be the ‘gas target’ defined in EIP1559 if that’s implemented in time. Wouldn't the actual limit (ie. twice the target) make the most sense here? > TIMESTAMP will be system time when the eth1-evm is processing the block Shouldn't post-merge TIMESTAMP just return GENESIS_TIME + slot_number * 12? There is going to be a bit of friction involving BLOCKHASH Because today BLOCKHASH is often used as a source of randomness Whereas in eth2 it will be trivial to grind But I guess there it's just dapps' responsibility to upgrade > `max_pow_block_num + slot` makes a lot of sense > Shouldn't post-merge TIMESTAMP just return GENESIS_TIME + slot_number * 12? Originally we were trying to be as much conservative as we can in terms of changes in EVM that are required by the merge. Since there is an option to embed eth1 block data into beacon block it makes sense to revisit concerns regarding EVM updates as well. hmm, I feel like there is a choice of which layer of abstraction you're importing. One option is to call process_block, but the other option is to call process_tx Or am I misunderstanding how the engine works? It currently processes the block as a whole, as if it would be a regular eth1 block w/o ethash data, this is why preserving eth1 block's format is the easiest path. We may pass timestamp, block number, block hash to `insertBlock` invocation, but that would require additional work done on the engine side.

excerpts.content:
> `max_pow_block_num + slot` makes a lot of sense
> Shouldn't post-merge TIMESTAMP just return GENESIS_TIME + slot_number * 12?
Originally we were trying to be as much conservative as we can in terms of changes in EVM that are required by the merge. Since there is an option to embed eth1 block data into beacon block it makes sense to revisit concerns regarding EVM updates as well.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: It currently processes the block as a whole, as if it would be a regular eth1 block w/o ethash data, this is why preserving eth1 block's format is the easiest path. We may pass timestamp, block number, block hash to `insertBlock` invocation, but that would require additional work done on the engine side.
